sentences.text: That on 23.10.2021 between 9.30 to 10.30 a.m. accused being the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-04-MT-6670 drove the same within the jurisdiction of R.T. Nagar Traffic Police station on Boopasandra Main road from K2 bus stand towards Boopasandra at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and near Chikoo farm hit to C.W.3 when she was sweeping on the right side of the road and also hit to 2 two wheelers bearing No.KA-04-EY-5280 and KA-13-S-770 which were proceeding from Boopasandra towards Hebbala.

As a result, Sri.Kumar Veerappan rider of two wheeler bearing No.KA-04-EY-5280 fell down and sustained grievous and succumbed to death at spot and rider/C.W.1 and pillion CC No.2249/2022 rider/C.W.2 of two wheeler bearing No.KA-13-S-770 fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Further, after the accident accused has failed to provide medical assistance to the injured and also failed to inform the same to the nearest police station.
As such the accused has committed an offence punishable U/Sec.279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC & Sec.134(A & B) R/w Sec.187 of IMV Act.
3. Cognizance was taken by perusing the prosecution papers and materials, the accused on receipt of summons appeared before the court and got himself enlarged on bail.

On the said date the prosecution papers were furnished to the accused as per Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. and substance of accusation in the form of plea was read over and explained to him, accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
4.
During the course of trial the prosecution has examined PWs.1 to 5 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 16.
The statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded the accused had no explanation and he denied the incriminating circumstances appearing against him.
Heard both sides.

sentences.text: In order to bring home the charge against the accused the prosecution has examined 5 witnesses as PWs.1 to 5 and got marked Ex.
P.1 to 16
. Ex.P.1 & 2 are the 2 photos, Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar,

Ex.P.4 is the statement of P.W.2, Ex.P.5 is the complaint, Ex.P.6 is the statement of P.W.5, Ex.P.7 is the FIR, Ex.P.8 is the rough sketch, Ex.P.9 is the inquest mahazar, Ex.P.10 is the PM report, Ex.P.11 & 12 are the notice and reply U/Sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P.12 is the indemnity bond, Ex.P.13 is the indemnity bond, Ex.P.4 is the IMV report and Ex.P.15 & 16 are the wound certificates.
11. Before adverting to the appreciation of evidence it is proper to state in brief the evidence deposed by the prosecution witnesses.
12. C.W.2 examined as P.W.1 is the one of the victim of this case.

He deposed that, on 23.10.2021 between 9.45 to 10.30 a.m. he and C.W.1 were proceeding in two wheeler from Boopasandra towards Hebbala and at that time he was the pillion rider and CC No.2249/2022 C.W.1 was riding the two wheeler and near K2 bus stand one car bearing No.MT-6670 came at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and came to extreme right and firstly hit to one two wheeler which was proceeding in their front and secondly hit to their two wheeler.
As a result he and C.W.1 fell down and both sustained fractures and rider of another two wheeler succumbed to death at spot.
After the accident he and C.W.1 took treatment at Bowring hospital.

Further he deposed that, accident has occurred due to the fault of the driver of offending vehicle and after the accident driver of the offending vehicle went away from the spot by leaving the vehicle at spot.
In his cross examination he has admitted that, he has not seen the driver of the car at the time of the accident and he is seeing the accused for the first time in the Court.
13. C.W.4 examined as P.W.2 is the eye witness to the incident.

He deposed that, C.W.1 and 2 are his relatives and on 23.10.2021 C.W.1 informed about the accident to him through phone, by receiving the information he went to spot and he shifted C.W.1 and 2 CC No.2249/2022 to hospital through an ambulance.

After enquiring C.W.1, he informed that, when he was proceeding along with pillion rider C.W.2 from Boopasandra towards Hebbala, on Boopasandra main road one Toyota Fortuner car came in high speed and hit to one Dio vehicle and further hit to their vehicle and rider of Dio vehicle succumbed to death at spot and accident occurred due to the fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
On the next day of the accident police conducted spot mahazar/Ex.P.3 at accident spot and obtained his signature on it.
In his cross examination he admitted that, the police have conducted the mahazar 2 to 3 days after the accident.
He has stated that, he has not seen the accused.
14. C.W.1 examined as P.W.3 is another victim of this case.

He deposed that, on 23.10.2021 between 9.30 to 10.00 a.m. he and C.W.2 were proceeding in his two wheeler bearing No.KA-30-S-7770 from Boopasandra towards Hebbala and at that time he was riding the two wheeler and C.W.2 was the pillion rider and near Chikoo farm one car bearing No.6670 came and firstly hit to one CC No.2249/2022 Dio two wheeler which was proceeding in their front and secondly hit to their two wheeler.
As a result he and C.W.2 sustained fractures and rider of another two wheeler succumbed to death at spot.
After the accident he informed same to C.W.4 and he shifted them to Bowring hospital.
With this regard he has lodged a complaint as per Ex.P.5.

Further he deposed that,
accident has occurred due to the fault of the driver of offending vehicle as he came to extreme right Rt Nagar Tr Ps vs Uday Y M on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134434593/
4 negligently and hit to their vehicle.
In his cross examination he has stated that, he has seen the accused at spot.
He has denied the suggestion that, he has lodged the complaint 2 days after the accident.
He has denied the suggestion that, he has filed a false complaint in order to obtain compensation.
15. C.W.3 examined as P.W.4 is the another victim of this case.
She deposed that, she is working as scavenger at BBMP ward No.21.
On 24.0.2021 at 9.30 a.m. when she was sweeping one car hit to her and after that she was unconscious and when she got consciousness at Gangenahalli government hospital and CC No.2249/2022
she sustained injuries on her left leg.
Further police took her statement at hospital and she signed on Ex.P.3 at police station and she does not know the contents of Ex.P.3.
Learned APP treated her as hostile witness and cross examined her in detail but nothing is elicited from her to disbelieve her examination in chief.
16 . C.W.18 examined as P.W.5 is the Investigating Officer and he has deposed about the investigation conducted by him.
In the cross examination he has stated that, he has not enquired the owner of the car regarding number of drivers to the offending car.
He has stated that, he does not know if the owner of the car has 5 cars and 4 drivers.
He has denied the suggestion that, he has colluded with the owner of the car and filed a false case against the accused.
17. With the above evidence, this court has to ascertain whether the prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts.

In order to CC No.2249/2022 prove offence U/Sec.279 of IPC the prosecution has to prove;
(i) Rash and negligent driving on public way (ii) The act must be such as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.
18. To prove an offence U/sec.304(A) of IPC the prosecution has to prove;
i) death of a person.
ii) the death occurred due to the rash or negligent act of the accused person.
iii) there must be an absence of an intention to cause death iv) there must be a direct link between the rash and negligent act and death of the victim.
19.
After marshalling all the oral and documentary evidence it is crystal clear that, there is dispute about the accused driving the offending car on the date of the accident.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the accused that, none of the witnesses are able to identify the accused and the prosecution has not proved CC No.2249/2022 that the accused was driving the offending vehicle at the time of the accident.
It is the contention of the accused that, the police have fixed the accused in a false case.
Further it is contended by the accused counsel that, owner of the offending car has 5 cars and 4 drivers and accused is one of the drivers.

It is submitted that, the accused was not driving Rt Nagar Tr Ps vs Uday Y M on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134434593/
5 the offending vehicle on the date of the accident.

sentences.text: It is contended that, the police have fixed the accused in a false case by colluding with the owner of the car.
20. On perusal of entire evidence it is seen that the eye witnesses i.e., P.W.1, 3 and 5 have not identified the accused.

In order to prove that the accused was driving the offending vehicle at the time of the accident, the prosecution has submitted the notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply under the said provision as Ex.P.11 and 12.
In Ex.P.12 reply given to the notice it is stated by the owner of the car C.W.11 that the accused was driving the vehicle at the time of the accident.
The learned counsel for the accused has consented to the marking of inquest, death memo, PM report, IMV report and notice and reply CC No.2249/2022 U/Sec.133 of IMV Act.
On his consent C.W.11 is dropped.
Hence, prosecution is able to prove that, the accused was driving the vehicle at the time of the accident.
In this case there is no dispute regarding the offending vehicle i.e., KA-04-MT-6670 causing the accident.
There is no dispute about the death of Kumar Veerappan who was the rider of two wheeler bearing No.KA-04-EY-5280.
As per P.M. report/Ex.P.10 the injuries are ante-mortem and death occurred due to severe head injuries leading to cardio respiratory arrest.
Hence, there is no dispute that the injuries were sustained by the deceased as a result of accident.
There is no dispute regarding IMV report as per Ex.P.14, which states that there is no mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.
Hence, the accident did not occur due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in the accident.
Since, the death of the Kumar Veerappan is not disputed and it is proved from the above discussion that the accused was driving the offending vehicle.
The Court only needs to consider if there was any negligence or rashness on the part of the accused due to which the accident occurred.
In order to prove rashness or negligence of the accused the prosecution has examined P.W.1, 3 and 5 who are the victims.
P.W.1, 3 and 5 have not stated anything regarding the rashness or negligence on the part of the accused.
They have vaguely stated that the car bearing No.6670 came in a high speed on the extreme right side of the road and in a negligent manner and hit them.
They have not stated the speed of the car.
P.W.3 who is the complainant in his complaint/Ex.P.5 has not stated anything about the car coming to the extreme right side of the road.
Even P.W.1 and 5 in their statement under Sec.161 of Cr.PC have not stated anything about the car coming to the extreme right side of the road and hitting the vehicles.
Hence, this is an improvement made by P.W.1 and 3 to attribute negligence to the accused.
Apart from the victim witnesses the prosecution has examined one eye witness i.e., P.W.2.
He has stated that, he arrived at the spot of the accident after receiving a call from P.W.3.
Hence, he has denied witnessing the accident.
Learned APP treated him as hostile and cross examined him in detail but nothing is elicited from him to disbelieve his examination CC No.2249/2022 in chief.
Therefore, apart from the victim witnesses there are no independent eye witnesses to the accident.
The victim witnesses are evidently interested witnesses as they stand to gain in terms of compensation if the accused is found guilty of rashness or negligence.
As already stated all the 3 victim witnesses have deposed vaguely regarding negligence of the accused.

Further they have deposed that, the accused came in a high speed but they have not specified the speed of Rt Nagar Tr Ps vs Uday Y M on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134434593/
6 the vehicle.

entities.text: Rt Nagar Tr Ps vs Uday Y M
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, from evidence of P.W.1, 3 and 5 the prosecution is not able to prove rashness or negligence on part of the accused.
22. Apart from the eye witnesses the prosecution is relying on documentary evidence.
In this regard the prosecution is relying on mahazar and rough sketch marked as Ex.P.3 and 8.
In order to prove the spot of accident police have conducted mahazar as per Ex.P.3 in presence of P.W.2 and 5.
As per Ex.P.3 mahazar said to have been conducted on 24.10.2023.
P.W.2 has stated that, he has identified the spot of the accident.
But he has signed Ex.P.3 in the police station.
P.W.5 has stated CC No.2249/2022 that, she has signed Ex.P.3 in the police station and she has not visited the spot with the police.
From Ex.P.3 it appears that the police have fixed the spot of accident on the say of P.W.2.
But P.W.2 is not an eye witness and he could not have fixed the spot of accident.
Further, rough sketch/Ex.P.8 does not indicate the spot where P.W.5 was standing at the time of the accident.
Hence, Ex.P.8/rough sketch is not reliable.
Further the prosecution is relying on IMV report as per Ex.P.14 which states the damages sustained by the car and there is no mechanical defect in the car and both the two wheelers.
But the IMV report by itself cannot aid in proving the guilt of the accused.
Prosecution is relying on PM report and the same does not indicate that the injuries occurred due to the negligence of accused.
Therefore, even the documentary evidence submitted by the prosecution does not prove the case of the prosecution.
Hence, this Court cannot proceed to convict the accused with the evidence available on record.
Moreover, merely because a vehicle was being driven at a high speed does not mean that the driver was driving rashly or negligently.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Karnataka V/s Sathish reported in 1998 SCC (Cri) 1508 has stated that, driving at a high speed by itself does not imply negligence or rashness.

entities.text: State of Karnataka V/s Sathish reported in 1998 SCC (Cri) 1508
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Negligence or rashness would have to be established as a fact.
There is only a bare statement made by P.W.1 and 3 that the offending vehicle was driven at a high speed and rash manner.
No attempt has been made to establish that there was rashness on the part of the accused.
The expression high speed could range from 30 k.m. per hour to 100 k.m. per hour.
The speed limit in the particular road is also not on record.
Therefore in absence of material fact merely because P.W.1 and 3 have alleged that accused was driving at a high speed it cannot be said that the accused is guilty of rash or negligent act.

24. Reference may be taken from the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case titled "Mohammed Aynuddin @ Miyan vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, reported in (200) 07 SCC 72,
wherein the CC No.2249/2022 Hon'ble Apex Court discussed in detail the constituents of a "rash or negligent act" and observed:

entities.text: Mohammed Aynuddin @ Miyan vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, reported in (200) 07 SCC 72
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "A rash act is primarily an over hasty act.
It is opposed to a deliberate act.
Still a rash act can be a deliberate act in the sense that it was done without due care and caution.
Culpable rashness lies in running the risk of doing an act with recklessness and with indifference as to the consequences.
Criminal negligence is the failure to exercise duty with reasonable and proper care and precaution guarding against injury to the public generally or to any individual in particular.

It is the imperative duty of the Rt Nagar Tr Ps vs Uday Y M on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134434593/
7 driver of a vehicle to adopt such reasonable and proper care and precaution."

entities.text: Rt Nagar Tr Ps vs Uday Y M on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further it is held that it is wrong to presume rashness or negligence on part of the driver for any motor accident.
25. Therefore, indifference to the consequences of one's act or absence of reasonable care and precaution is the most important ingredient constituting rashness or negligence.

It should be noted that intention of the person acting rash or negligent act is immaterial and what is important is that he has not taken due care or has done the said act with indifference to the consequences.
Further, it should be noted that there should be direct nexus between the act or rashness or negligence and hurt/grievous hurt/death, as the case may be, suffered by the victim.
In this case only P.W.1 and 3 have deposed that the accused had driven the car at a high speed without specifying the speed.

26. By ascertaining all these oral and documentary evidence it is clear that, there is no substantive,
cogent and corroborative evidence to prove the guilt of the CC No.2249/2022 accused.

Therefore, by considering the overall facts and circumstances of this case, this court is of the considered view that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.

Hence,
point Nos.1 and 2 are answered in the Negative.
27. The prosecution has also alleged that, the accused not informed police station or given first aid to the injured after the accident.
In this case the accused is not denying the accident or the death of Kumar Veerappan.
Admittedly the accused has not taken the injured to the hospital.
The main aim of Sec.134(A & B) is to ensure that the injured persons get timely medical help so that their life can be saved.
But in this case even though the accused is not at fault he had a duty to provide medical help to the injured and also inform the same to the nearest police station.
Hence, point No.3 answered in the affirmative.

Negligence or rashness would have to be established as a fact.
There is only a bare statement made by P.W.1 and 3 that the offending vehicle was driven at a high speed and rash manner.
No attempt has been made to establish that there was rashness on the part of the accused.
The expression high speed could range from 30 k.m. per hour to 100 k.m. per hour.
The speed limit in the particular road is also not on record.
Therefore in absence of material fact merely because P.W.1 and 3 have alleged that accused was driving at a high speed it cannot be said that the accused is guilty of rash or negligent act.
It should be noted that intention of the person acting rash or negligent act is immaterial and what is important is that he has not taken due care or has done the said act with indifference to the consequences.
Further, it should be noted that there should be direct nexus between the act or rashness or negligence and hurt/grievous hurt/death, as the case may be, suffered by the victim.
26. By ascertaining all these oral and documentary evidence it is clear that, there is no substantive,
cogent and corroborative evidence to prove the guilt of the CC No.2249/2022 accused.
Therefore, by considering the overall facts and circumstances of this case, this court is of the considered view that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
In this case the accused is not denying the accident or the death of Kumar Veerappan.
The main aim of Sec.134(A & B) is to ensure that the injured persons get timely medical help so that their life can be saved.
But in this case even though the accused is not at fault he had a duty to provide medical help to the injured and also inform the same to the nearest police station.
